# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md — System of Work Assistant

> **Phase note.** Spec-anchored build plan decomposed from the binding `ARCHITECTURE.md` (production-grade). 26 phases (0–25), ~310 first-class tasks — Phases 14–25 = the Part II activation roadmap (ARCH §19; 66 gaps→tasks coverage-verified). The §3 contracts phase (Phase 1) was the forced-serial bottleneck; the §9 workflows phase (Phase 7) is the integration spine. Locked decisions live in `docs/planning/DECISIONS.md`; every phase anchors to `ARCHITECTURE.md §` sections — drift surfaces at TDD Step 9. **All task states in this file were verified against the repo (commits, symbols, tests, audits, green gates) on 2026-07-19 at baseline `db45eb6e`** — the doc-wide reverification that rebuilt this file to the format contract below.

> **Reading discipline.** Read by section, not whole. Round history lives in `docs/archive/IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md`, never here.

> **Session protocol:**
> - **Session start** — orchestrator `/orchestrate-start`; implementer `/session-start`. Confirm the session target.
> - **Session end** — implementer `/session-end` (TDD + cross-doc audit + Step-9 list + `/preflight`); orchestrator `/orchestrate-end` (reconcile State lines, Carry-forward, archive Log entry, push).

> **Format contract (lint-enforced by `scripts/plan-lint.sh`).**
> - **Task state** lives on ONE checkbox line — the first content line under each `### N.M` heading:
>   `- [x] DONE · `hash` · YYYY-MM-DD` (append `· dormant` for built-behind-OFF-flag work, `— arms via §ARM-x` where an arming ledger applies) · `- [~] PARTIAL · landed: …; remaining: … → target` · `- [ ] OPEN` · `- [ ] DEFERRED → target · owner-approved ref` · `- [ ] OWNER-GATED ⛔ Owner-Gates §ARM-x`.
>   Headings carry **no** state tokens; metadata (`**Kind:** / **Spec:** / **Depends:** / **Blocks:** / **Files:**`) are plain fielded lines, never checkboxes; narrative never carries state.
> - **Currently in progress** — ≤3 items / ≤15 lines, REPLACED each round (a snapshot of NOW, not a history).
> - **Carry-forward** — ≤7 items; resolved items are DELETED (never annotated in place); overflow lives in the owning phase's `#### Residuals`.
> - **Owner gates & arming ledgers** — the dedicated section below; every `OWNER-GATED` task references a `§ARM-*`/`§DEC-*` id defined there.
> - **Every task** carries a `**Spec:**` `ARCHITECTURE.md §` anchor or an explicit `arch_gap` flag.
> - **Phase-exit checklists** live in the archive (`docs/archive/IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md` Part 3); each phase keeps a one-line `**Gate:**` pointer.

> **Spec-anchor convention.** Each phase header carries `**Spec anchors:**`, a `**Track:**` tag, and a `**Depends on (phases):**` edge. A slice surfacing a behavior the anchors don't cover is a cross-doc invariant flag at Step 9. New mid-build tasks get a first-class `### N.M` heading at the round they land — never narrative-only state.

### 1.2 — JSON Schema validation gate + schema registry
- [x] DONE · `8a42f133` · 2026-06-30

**Files:** packages/contracts/src/schema/registry.ts; packages/domain/src/validation/schema-gate.ts
The candidate-data gate (safety rule 2). A schema registry maps schemaId→compiled validator; an unknown schemaId is a typed rejection, never a silent pass-through. validate(output, schemaId) returns a typed Result — on failure it yields schemaId + failing JSON paths and does NOT return the output as usable, enforcing candidate-data-in/validated-out before any downstream use. ajv strict + format assertions reject unknown/additional properties so provider drift cannot smuggle fields; validation is pure/deterministic (no network/clock), and rejection variants are enumerable so the §9 meeting validator surfaces a distinct schema_rejected class.

## Phase 3 — Policy, Security & Egress (§5)
**Goal:** Build packages/policy as the security-critical decision core behind §6/§7/§8 — workspace-policy resolution, provider×capability matrix, EgressPolicy with the Employer-Work raw-egress VETO, ToolPolicy + ING-7 admission, approval policy, visibility enforcement — all typed, fail-closed, audit-emitting, redaction-safe PolicyDecisions, plus the renderer↔worker session-token auth primitive (loopback binding ≠ auth); the four hard denials are load-bearing and fail-closed by construction. · **Spec anchors:** §5 (primary) · §2.5 DAG/tracks · §3 frozen contracts · §7 broker/egress-veto ordering · §16 error-handling/redaction/observability · Appendix A · **Track:** providers-integrations · **Depends on (phases):** 1
**Gate:** ✅ /phase-exit 3 CLEAR (2026-07-01) — checklist: docs/archive/IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md Part 3 · audits: docs/audits/phase3-arch-drift.md, docs/audits/phase3-security.md

### 3.1 — Policy foundation: typed PolicyDecision + four-hard-denial taxonomy + denial audit/health/redaction contract
- [x] DONE · `bc18914b` · 2026-07-01
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §5 · REQ-NF-001 · **Depends:** P1 (§3 contracts frozen) · **Blocks:** 3.2–3.7
**Files:** packages/policy/{package.json, src/decision.ts, src/denials.ts, src/audit-signal.ts, src/index.ts}
Typed PolicyDecision<T> with explicit allow/deny variants; every deny carries a stable closed-set DenialReason code, human message, and the refs/hashes to build an AuditRecord (§16 typed-result — nothing fails silently). Enumerates exactly the four §5 hard-denial codes: EMPLOYER_RAW_EGRESS_UNACKNOWLEDGED, DIRECT_CROSS_WORKSPACE_RAW_RETRIEVAL, UNTRUSTED_CONTENT_MUTATING_TOOL (ING-7), WRITE_ADAPTER_OUTSIDE_GATEWAY — an unknown/unmapped reason is a programming-error reject, never a silent allow. Fail-closed by construction: any missing/unrecognized/malformed input resolves to DENY (default-deny is the contract, not a convention). Each denial maps to an AuditRecord + a distinct persistent audit-linked typed System-Health signal class (OBS-2); the decision payload is redaction-safe — refs/hashes/processor-ids/codes only, never raw content, prompts, or credential-shaped strings. WRITE_ADAPTER_OUTSIDE_GATEWAY enforced structurally via import-direction (§2.5); no invented runtime token.

- [x] DONE · `bc18914b` · 2026-07-01

Resolves a Workspace (type, dataOwner, defaultVisibility, egressPolicy, providerMatrix) into one pure/deterministic typed view for the matrix/egress/approval steps. Visibility taxonomy is the closed set isolated|coordination|sanitized|full; a GclProjection whose visibilityLevel exceeds the source workspace's defaultVisibility or falls outside the set is rejected on validation. Edge: a projection whose sourceWorkspace mismatches its workspaceId, or that omits a declared visibility level/source workspace, is rejected (§3 universal rule).

### 3.3 — Provider × capability matrix evaluation → ProviderRoute resolution
- [x] DONE · `bc18914b` · 2026-07-01
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §5 (route feeds §7 veto) · REQ-S-005 · **Depends:** 3.1, 3.2 · **Blocks:** 3.4
**Files:** packages/policy/src/provider-matrix.ts
Resolves the ProviderRoute for an AgentJob (workspaceId, capability) from the workspace ProviderMatrix's capabilityDefaults[capability]; a capability with no configured route is a typed DENY with a distinct reason — there is NO implicit/global fallback route. Only providers in allowedProviders are eligible (a capabilityDefault pointing outside the allowlist is rejected); resolution is pure and deterministic and performs NO health/availability/budget checks (those are the §7 broker, after route resolution and after the egress veto). The resolved route surfaces egressClass + processor identity for the downstream egress veto (3.4): local Ollama/LM Studio routes are non-egress, cloud and OpenRouter routes carry their processor id. Edge: a local-class route whose endpoint is outside explicit local-provider config is rejected — no arbitrary provider URL is accepted (pins §5 'local endpoints only through explicit local-provider config'; prototype-member fail-open closed via Object.hasOwn).

### 3.4 — EgressPolicy enforcement + Employer-Work raw-content egress VETO (hard denial #1)
- [x] DONE · `bc18914b` · 2026-07-01
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §5, §7 veto ordering · REQ-S-002, REQ-S-005, REQ-F-001 · **Depends:** 3.1, 3.2, 3.3
**Files:** packages/policy/src/{egress.ts, processors.ts}; test/adversarial-regressions.test.ts
Egress is evaluated AFTER provider selection and acts strictly as a VETO over the resolved ProviderRoute — it can only narrow or deny, never widen (closes the 'matrix bypasses egress' gap, §7 ordering). Processor model: every cloud LLM endpoint, OpenRouter, and Drive/NotebookLM is a distinct ProcessorId; OpenRouter is its OWN processor, NOT an OpenAI-compatible alias; local Ollama/LM Studio are non-egress. A route's processor must be in allowedProcessors, and when the job carries raw content it must ADDITIONALLY be in rawContentAllowedProcessors, else deny. Employer-Work raw-egress veto: for an Employer-Work AgentJob carrying raw content with employerRawEgressAcknowledged=false, the ONLY eligible route is a loopback-local (non-egress) provider; absent a conformant local provider the job FAILS CLOSED (EMPLOYER_RAW_EGRESS_UNACKNOWLEDGED) — no cloud fallback. Acknowledgment ON lifts the veto only for rawContentAllowedProcessors; toggling OFF re-blocks on the next job — re-evaluation is per-job, idempotent, no cached allow. Edge: a remote/proxied/non-loopback URL presented as 'local' is treated as egress (closes the tunneled-local hole; loopback-spoof bypass found by adversarial verify + fixed with regression tests).

### 3.5 — ToolPolicy evaluation + ING-7 untrusted-content job-admission gate (hard denial #3)
- [x] DONE · `bc18914b` · 2026-07-01
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §5 (ING-7) · REQ-S-001 · **Depends:** 3.1
**Files:** packages/policy/src/{tool-policy.ts, admission.ts}
The admission predicate runs at job admission (Agent Job created → admitted), BEFORE provider selection / running / egress veto — a rejection here prevents the job from ever reaching a provider or producing any side effect. For any AgentJob whose context is untrusted content, if its ToolPolicy admits a mutating tool (allowsMutating=true, OR allowedTools contains a mutating tool, OR mode='scoped_write'), the job is REJECTED at admission (UNTRUSTED_CONTENT_MUTATING_TOOL, ING-7) — a hard reject, not a silent downgrade. ToolPolicy evaluation is closed and deny-wins: a tool in deniedTools is never admitted even if also in allowedTools; mode='read_only' forces effective allowsMutating=false regardless of declared tools. Untrusted-content classification is an explicit typed input (supplied by the §9 workflow); a job lacking a trust/sensitivity classification is treated as untrusted (fail-closed default). A rejected admission emits an AuditRecord + a distinct typed System-Health item and guarantees no provider call or side effect occurred. admitCandidateJob composes ajv + Zod.refine + admitJob (the full candidate-data gate).

### 3.6 — Approval policy evaluation (requiresApproval predicate + card parameters)
- [x] DONE · `bc18914b` · 2026-07-01
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §5 · REQ-F-012 · **Depends:** 3.1, 3.2
**Files:** packages/policy/src/approval-policy.ts; test/approval-policy.test.ts
Decides requiresApproval for a ProposedAction / ExternalWriteEnvelope from its targetSystem, approvalPolicy, the workspace visibility/egress posture (3.2), and dataOwner; a missing or ambiguous policy defaults to requiresApproval=true (fail-closed — never auto-apply under uncertainty). Shared / invite / external-message / cross-workspace-visible actions ALWAYS require approval; only private, policy-allowed personal actions may be auto-allowed (pins Flow 3 auto-create-private-only and Flow 6; auto-allow is keyed off an explicit AUTO_ALLOW_ELIGIBLE_TARGETS allow-list). Emits the approval-card parameters §9 needs — required channel(s), card visibility level, and deferred defaults (re-surface after a snooze, default 24h; auto-expire after a window, default 7d) — but the predicate does NOT mutate Approval state (the idempotent transition is §9). Pure and deterministic and redaction-safe (payloadHash/refs, never the raw payload).

### 3.7 — Renderer↔worker auth primitive: per-launch session-token mint/inject/verify + Origin/Host allowlist
- [x] DONE · `bc18914b` · 2026-07-01
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §5, §13 topology · REQ-S-004, REQ-NF-004 · **Depends:** 3.1
**Files:** packages/policy/src/session-auth.ts (pure verify + Origin/Host allowlist); apps/desktop/main/session-token.ts (mint); wiring landed Phase 7/9 under apps/worker/src/api/auth/* + apps/desktop/preload/bridge.ts
Electron main mints a per-LAUNCH session token that is high-entropy (CSPRNG randomBytes(32), not derived from any guessable value), regenerated every launch, never persisted plaintext, never logged. The token reaches the renderer ONLY via preload (contextIsolation on, no Node integration) — never a window global, query string, or world-readable file discoverable by another localhost client. The worker API requires the token on EVERY tRPC call AND on the WS/SSE stream handshake; a missing/wrong/expired token is rejected BEFORE any handler or business logic runs (authentication precedes dispatch/authorization). A strict Origin/Host allowlist rejects cross-origin / DNS-rebinding callers — loopback binding alone is explicitly NOT authentication (REQ-NF-004 binding, not auth). Comparison is constant-time (timingSafeEqual, no timing leak); rejection paths emit an auth-failure audit + health signal and never echo the token. A stale token from a previous launch is rejected (per-launch lifecycle, consistent with worker re-spawn, §16 supervision). The plan-named app-shell paths (apps/worker/src/api/auth-guard.ts, apps/desktop/preload/inject-token.ts) were an owner-approved deferment to Phase 7/9 and landed under auth/* + bridge.ts; functionality fully realized, only the paths differ.

### Acceptance criteria (3)
- [x] DONE · `bc18914b` · 2026-07-01 · closes /phase-exit 3
Every policy decision is a typed, allow/deny-explicit PolicyDecision, fail-closed on missing/malformed input, emitting an AuditRecord + a distinct typed System-Health class with redaction-safe payloads (refs/hashes/codes only). The four §5 hard denials are enforced and non-bypassable: Employer-Work raw cloud egress with ack=false (loopback-local-only or fail-closed, no cloud fallback), direct cross-workspace raw retrieval (GCL-projection-only except approved Level-3 links), ING-7 untrusted-content jobs declaring mutating tools (rejected at admission), and the declared write-adapter-outside-gateway code. Egress is a post-selection pure veto (narrow/deny only); OpenRouter is its own processor; local Ollama/LM Studio are non-egress; non-loopback 'local' endpoints are egress; ack ON/OFF re-evaluates per-job with no cached allow. Matrix resolution is deterministic, allowlist-bound, no implicit fallback. The worker API rejects every unauthenticated/wrong-token/expired/wrong-Origin caller before any handler, with a per-launch token injected only via preload and constant-time verified. All §5 logic lives behind packages/policy over the §3-frozen seam models; §6/§7/§8 depend on these predicates.

## Phase 4 — Knowledge: Markdown, Obsidian, GBrain & GCL

**Goal:** Knowledge track of §6 — KnowledgeWriter as the provably-sole autonomous semantic-Markdown writer (validated KnowledgeMutationPlan apply; human-section preservation; reject-not-redact secret scan; compare-revision precondition; atomic commit; audit + async GBrain sync), per-vault fs-watch out-of-band reconciliation, a read/query-only GBrain adapter (parity-quarantine + rebuild-from-Markdown + version-pin), the fail-closed write-through layer, and the GCL Visibility Gate. Markdown stays canonical; GBrain derived/rebuildable; persists via repository interfaces (no concrete driver). · **Spec anchors:** §6 (PRIMARY) · §3 universal rules · §2.5 · §12 · §16 · Appendix A · **Track:** knowledge · **Depends on (phases):** 1, 3
**Gate:** ✅ /phase-exit 4 CLEAR (2026-07-01) — checklist: docs/archive/IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md Part 3 · audits: docs/audits/phase4-arch-drift.md, docs/audits/phase4-security.md

### 4.1 — KnowledgeWriter core: validated-plan apply, atomic commit, compare-revision precondition, revision/audit recording, sole-writer invariant
- [x] DONE · `84c3c7e2` · 2026-07-01
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §6 · REQ-S-006 · REQ-F-006 · §16 · **Depends:** P1 (§3 contracts) · **Blocks:** 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.14
**Files:** packages/knowledge/src/knowledge-writer/writer.ts, revision.ts; markdown-vault/atomic-write.ts
Accepts ONLY a schema-valid KnowledgeMutationPlan carrying workspaceId + sourceRefs — a plan failing the JSON-Schema gate (REQ-S-006) or missing them is rejected before any filesystem touch (no partial write). Sole-writer invariant (REQ-F-006, KN-4/9): this is the only path that mutates a workspace Markdown repo, exposing no bypass and no raw-write export. Atomic all-or-nothing across the whole plan at exactly one new revision id or nothing; compare-revision precondition fails a typed write_conflict on base drift (no lost update). One AuditRecord per commit (revision, actor, source event, WorkflowRunRef, idempotencyKey, before/after); idempotent replay by idempotencyKey never double-commits. Every failure is typed (schema_rejected/write_conflict/ownership_violation/secret_found) and routed to outbox/System Health, never silent.

A per-vault watcher detects external working-tree changes (Obsidian Sync / iCloud / git pull — a supported V1 config) and recomputes the on-disk revision id. A clean external change advances the base/compare revision so subsequent applies precondition against the new revision (external edits not clobbered); a conflicting concurrent change (KW pending vs external) yields a System Health conflict-review item, never a silent lost update. Positive KnowledgeWriter attribution (write-through GO #1, REQ-S-NEW-008): each mutation is matched against a kw_writer_sig + write-journal — any mutation that is neither a verified KW write nor a human-owned-REGION edit, INCLUDING a new assistant-domain file, becomes conflict-review and NEVER auto-advances the base (closes the out-of-band hidden-brain hole); a human-REGION edit still clean-advances. Wake/restart ordering (LIFE-6): pending KW writes apply before queued index jobs (re-derive by revision id); debounced so one sync burst = one revision recompute.

## Phase 5 — Provider & Runtime Broker

**Goal:** Two-layer Provider & Runtime Broker executing governed AgentJobs — a ModelProviderPort (raw schema-validated extraction: Claude/OpenAI/OpenRouter/Ollama/LM Studio) + an AgentRuntimePort (Claude Agent SDK + Hermes), fronted by a Broker that resolves the workspace×capability matrix and applies a fixed gate order (egress veto → health/availability → budget caps → schema/tool-policy), normalizing every output into a capability schema and emitting only KnowledgeMutationPlan/ProposedAction candidates — no provider output ever calls a write adapter. · **Spec anchors:** §7 (primary); §2.5, §3, §5, §12, §13, §16, Appendix A · **Track:** providers-integrations · **Depends on (phases):** 1, 3
**Gate:** ✅ /phase-exit 5 CLEAR (2026-07-01) — checklist: docs/archive/IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md Part 3 · audits: docs/audits/phase5-arch-drift.md, docs/audits/phase5-security.md

"Claude" is intentionally two adapters — a Claude Agent SDK runtime vs a Claude model provider — and one adapter MUST NOT satisfy both ports. AgentResult.logs is an isolated field that 5.6 redaction is contractually required to strip before any sink. Ports import only §3 contracts (AgentJob/Capability/ProviderRoute/ToolPolicy/outputSchemaId), zero write-adapter (knowledge/integrations) import — pinned by an architectural import test.

### 5.2 — Broker route resolution + ordered gate pipeline + AgentJob lifecycle state machine
- [x] DONE · `ac9f9b8d` · 2026-07-01
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §7, §5, DOMAIN_MODEL AgentJob machine · **Depends:** 5.1, P3 (§5 matrix resolution + ING-7 admission) · **Blocks:** 5.3, 5.4, 5.5, 5.9

Route is resolved SOLELY from ProviderMatrix.capabilityDefaults[capability] for the job's workspace — no hard-wired reference runtime; any conformance-passing provider/runtime is routable. Gates run in EXACTLY this order (reordering is a defect): matrix route → egress veto → health/availability → budget caps → schema/tool-policy, with the egress veto AFTER selection (a veto, not a pre-filter). Drives created→admitted→provider_selected→running→schema_validated→accepted (branches rejected|cancelled_budget|failed_retryable|failed_terminal); skipping admitted/provider_selected is forbidden. No eligible provider after the sequence → fail closed with a typed failure + distinct System Health item, never a silent fallback; re-drive on the same idempotencyKey is replay-safe (no duplicate audit/candidate) and an admitted job's ToolPolicy is binding and never relaxed. An adversarial regression pins runRoute===budgetRoute===MATRIX_ROUTE (no divergent-route exfil). The no-eligible-provider health class is a broker-local named constant (arch_gap) absent from the frozen FailureClass enum — see Residuals.

## Phase 6 — Connector & Tool Gateways

**Goal:** providers-integrations external edge — a Connector Gateway owning ALL external READS (per-connector cursors, bounded-backoff retry, typed health, unreachable queue/hold/drain-in-order, no silent drops) and a Tool Gateway as the ONLY external-WRITE path via the external-write envelope (idempotencyKey + canonicalObjectKey + pre-write existence check + persisted receipt, replay-safe) plus a write outbox and the NotebookPort Drive-backed 00–04 managed-doc sync; invariant cores (no-silent-drop reads, no-duplicate writes) land before adapter breadth. · **Spec anchors:** §8, §3, §5, §16, §9, §15, Appendix A · PRD §20.1 replay gate · REQ-I-004/I-005/F-010/F-012/F-014/NF-006 · **Track:** providers-integrations · **Depends on (phases):** 1, 3
**Gate:** ✅ /phase-exit 6 CLEAR (2026-07-01) — checklist: docs/archive/IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md Part 3 · audits: docs/audits/phase6-arch-drift.md, docs/audits/phase6-security.md

### 6.1 — Connector Gateway core read engine (cursors, backoff, health, unreachable branch)
- [x] DONE · `eb19898b` · 2026-07-01
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §8 / REQ-I-005 (cursor no-silent-drop); §16 (backoff/degraded/OBS-2/Keychain/redaction); LIFE-6/LIFE-4 (wake/reconnect) · **Depends:** P1, P3 · **Blocks:** 6.3
**Files:** packages/integrations/src/connectors/{gateway,port,backoff,health}.ts
Implements ConnectorPort reads: a sync advances a per-connector cursor persisted through the P1 operational-store repo only after the consumer commits, so a mid-stream failure NEVER advances past unprocessed records (no silent drops). Transient errors retry with bounded exponential backoff (capped attempts + max delay); on exhaustion the connector is marked degraded with a distinct, persistent, audit-linked System Health signal (OBS-2). The unreachable branch queues/holds inbound and drains in order on reconnect wired to LIFE-6 wake/power hooks, deduping replayed records by content-hash/cursor. Credentials resolve via Keychain references through the secrets broker (never plaintext in store or logs); Keychain-locked → degraded, dependent reads held-retryable until unlock. Health is a typed reachable | degraded | unreachable result; read logs route through the §16 redaction layer so raw content and credential-shaped strings never reach a log sink.

### 6.2 — Tool Gateway external-write envelope core (no-duplicate-write invariant)
- [x] DONE · `eb19898b` · 2026-07-01
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §5 fourth hard denial (no write adapter outside Tool Gateway); §3 (ExternalWriteEnvelope/canonical-key/idempotency); §8 — REQ-F-012, REQ-F-014 · **Depends:** P1, P3 · **Blocks:** 6.4, 6.5, 6.6
**Files:** packages/integrations/src/tools/{gateway,envelope,existence-check,receipt-store}.ts
Tool Gateway is the ONLY external-write path — adapters are invokable solely through the envelope flow and a write attempted outside it is rejected (§5 fourth hard denial). Each write builds an ExternalWriteEnvelope from the inbound ProposedAction (canonicalObjectKey + idempotencyKey + preconditions + payloadHash). A mandatory pre-write existence check matches by canonicalObjectKey and reuses the existing object + receipt on hit (vendor create-tools lack native idempotency) — no duplicate external write; concurrency-safe via an atomic reserve()/release() between the existence-check and the sole adapter.create call site. A replayed/retried envelope with the same idempotencyKey reuses the stored receipt or matched object and performs NO second side effect (externally exactly-once; PRD §20.1 / RISK-004). Approval-requiring actions record a pending Approval and do not dispatch until approved, then apply once idempotently across Mac/Telegram. A precondition mismatch routes to a typed retry/conflict, never a blind overwrite; every dispatch records an AuditRecord and persists the receipt through the §16 redaction layer.

- [x] DONE · `eb19898b` · 2026-07-01

Outbound writes attempted during a connector outage are HELD in the write outbox (persisted via the P1 repository interface) rather than failing or dropping (§8); each held item retains its full ExternalWriteEnvelope (idempotencyKey, canonicalObjectKey, payloadHash). The DRAIN now classifies the due depth it already lists and records a durable HealthItem; held items never silently expire. The drain entry-point is callable by the downstream §9 connector-sync/health and approval workflows; a crash mid-drain re-drives idempotently with no orphaned or double-applied writes.

Continuous auto-sync of arbitrary docs is NOT performed; a missing/unlinked managed source surfaces a typed 're-add/refresh NotebookLM source' state, not a silent failure. Direct NotebookLM API is out of scope (V1.1 / spike-gated, §15) — sync is Drive-backed only.

## Phase 7 — Temporal Workflows & Automation

**Goal:** Build the durable integration spine — a supervised Temporal worker owning all 13 core product workflows atop the lifecycle invariants (single-active-instance lease LIFE-1, collapsed-catch-up schedules LIFE-2, idempotent in-flight resume reusing the §8 external-write envelope LIFE-3/REQ-NF-006, clock-jump-safe bookkeeping LIFE-5). Every run is a WorkflowRun carrying an idempotencyKey + audit refs, enforces its DOMAIN_MODEL state machine, routes semantic writes only through KnowledgeWriter and external writes only through the Tool Gateway, surfaces each failure class as a distinct System Health item, and binds a workspace before any durable processing; Hermes automation is permitted but gateway-routed. · **Spec anchors:** §9 (primary) · §2.5 (worker-track DAG, structural) · §16 (lifecycle/supervision/observability/time) · §6 (KW/GCL/GBrain) · §8 (Connector/Tool/NotebookPort gateways) · §7 (Runtime Broker) · §5 (policy/admission) · §4 (operational store) · Appendix A (WorkflowRunRef, Approval, AgentJob, SourceEnvelope, ProposedAction, ExternalWriteEnvelope, KnowledgeMutationPlan, GclProjection) · DOMAIN_MODEL state machines · USER_FLOWS 1–7 · REQ-F-002/007–014/017/018, REQ-NF-006, REQ-S-007 · **Track:** worker · **Depends on (phases):** 2, 4, 5, 6
**Gate:** ✅ /phase-exit 7 CLEAR (2026-07-02) + Worker-wiring phase-exit CLEAR (2026-07-02) — checklist: docs/archive/IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md Part 3 · audits: docs/audits/phase7-arch-drift.md · phase7-security.md

### 7.1 — Temporal worker bootstrap + single-active-instance lease (LIFE-1)
- [x] DONE · `9a61db5` · 2026-07-01
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §16 (supervision) · §9 · REQ-NF-006 (LIFE-1) · **Depends:** P2 operational store, P-infra Temporal dev server (§13) · **Blocks:** 7.2, 7.4
**Files:** apps/worker/src/temporal/worker.ts · apps/worker/src/lease/instanceLease.ts · packages/workflows/src/runtime/taskQueue.ts
Worker connects to the local Temporal dev server with persistent (never in-memory) storage and registers the task queue; bootstrap is a typed result with explicit failure variants. Exactly one active instance may own the queue — a second concurrently-started instance fails to acquire the lease and stays passive (no split-brain); on supervised respawn the worker RE-ACQUIRES the lease before resuming dispatch and a stale lease clears at expiry. Temporal-unavailable is a first-class degraded mode: dispatch blocked, distinct System Health item surfaced, bounded-backoff retries — no crash-loop. Lease state persists in the operational store (P2), not Temporal history; nothing fails silently.

### 7.2 — Durable schedules + collapsed catch-up (LIFE-2) + clock-jump-safe bookkeeping (LIFE-5)
- [x] DONE · `9a61db5` · 2026-07-01
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §16 (Configuration & time) · REQ-NF-006 (LIFE-2/LIFE-5) · **Depends:** 7.1 · **Blocks:** 7.10, 7.11, 7.15, 7.19
**Files:** packages/workflows/src/runtime/schedule.ts · runtime/catchUpWindow.ts · runtime/clock.ts
A durable schedule abstraction registers recurring workflows (daily brief, weekly/monthly review, connector sync) with persisted last-run/next-run bookkeeping. On wake across multiple due occurrences the workflow runs exactly ONCE within the catch-up window — never once-per-missed-occurrence. Bookkeeping uses a monotonic clock where available and survives NTP/wall-clock correction (forward AND backward jump) without double-firing or starving — naive wall-clock comparison is rejected. Occurrences older than the configurable catch-up window are dropped as missed (recorded, surfaced as a missed/late-schedule health class), not silently replayed; registration and last-run advance are idempotent across restarts.

### 7.3 — In-flight workflow resume + external-write-envelope reuse (LIFE-3 / REQ-NF-006)

**Files:** packages/workflows/src/runtime/resume.ts · runtime/wakeHooks.ts · activities/envelopeReuse.ts
An in-flight workflow interrupted by restart/sleep/crash RESUMES from durable Temporal state without re-running committed steps; on resume every external side effect re-uses the SAME §8 ExternalWriteEnvelope (idempotencyKey + canonicalObjectKey + matched receipt) so a re-driven step performs NO duplicate external write (the §20.1 replay gate, proven create-then-restart-then-resume). Pending KnowledgeWriter writes apply BEFORE queued GBrain index jobs (§6 ordering); index jobs re-derive from current Markdown by revision id and never roll back a commit. Wake/power hooks (LIFE-6) drain held outbox work; a crashed-mid-flight activity retries idempotently with no partial side effect. Unrecoverable state surfaces a typed System Health item with its audit record rather than dropping the run.

### 8.1 — Worker-API auth gate: per-launch session-token verification + Origin/Host allowlist (loopback bind)
- [x] DONE · `745573f` · 2026-07-02
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §5 (per-launch token + Origin/Host allowlist L173), §10 Local App API (L303), REQ-NF-004 loopback bind, §16 redaction (L369) · **Depends:** none · **Blocks:** 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, 8.5
**Files:** apps/worker/src/api/auth/{sessionAuth,originAllowlist,loopbackBind}.ts (+ interceptor.ts, cors.ts)
A single transport interceptor verifies the §5 per-launch session token (constant-time compare) before any procedure/handler runs — missing/wrong token returns a typed unauthenticated error, handler never invoked. Both Origin and Host are checked against a strict allowlist so cross-origin, wrong-Host, and DNS-rebinding callers are rejected before any handler (distinct from the token check). The API binds loopback only — a non-loopback bind is a startup failure, not a warning. The token is never logged (reuses §16 redaction) nor echoed in error/rejection bodies; rejection emits an auditable security event that does not leak the expected token. This task consumes the token minted by Electron main / §5 policy — it verifies, never mints or persists it.

### 8.4 — Command procedures: approval transitions + ingestion-triage disposition (exactly-once / idempotent)
- [x] DONE · `745573f` · 2026-07-02
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §9 Approval state machine + workflow 8 (L281/L295), §7 one-writer + §8 Tool Gateway (dispatch-only), §11 Mac+Telegram parity (L313), workflow 5 ingestion-triage re-enter · **Depends:** 8.2, P7 (Approval flow + ingestion-triage workflows) · **Blocks:** 8.5, 8.7
**Files:** apps/worker/src/api/procedures/{commands,approvalCommands,triageCommands}.ts
Approval command supports approve/edit/reject/defer as single idempotent transitions over pending → approved|edited|rejected|deferred|expired; resubmitting the same decision is a no-op returning the same transition. Mac and Telegram are parity channels — the command path is the same idempotent transition regardless of channel, and a double-apply across both collapses to exactly one state change (applied:true, dispatch once). defer sets snoozeUntil/expiresAt and is non-terminal (deferred → pending|expired); an approve/reject on an already-expired item is a typed rejection with no state change, audited. Ingestion-inbox triage disposition re-enters the ingestion pipeline reusing the same idempotencyKey (replay-safe), resolving the ING-4 dead-end. Commands dispatch only to Temporal / the Tool Gateway via the worker — the API writes no external system or Markdown directly, preserving the one-writer / Tool-Gateway invariants.

### 8.5 — Single push stream: authenticated handshake + four event classes
- [x] DONE · `cd3a5da` · 2026-07-02

A single push stream (WS or SSE, per the Phase-0 API spike OQ-002) carries workflow status, approval updates, System Health, and read-model changes — one stream, four event classes. The handshake passes the same 8.1 session-token + Origin/Host allowlist gate; an unauthenticated or wrong-origin/wrong-Host handshake is rejected before any subscription is established. Stream payloads reuse the 8.2 UI-safe projection boundary so no secrets or raw content cross. Each event carries a correlation/workflow-run id and a monotonic per-stream sequence number (via tracked()/lastEventId) for client ordering and resume; approval-update events are exactly-once and consistent with the 8.4 transition — a replayed/resumed workflow produces no duplicate approval event.

### 8.6 — Stream reconnection + backpressure semantics
- [x] DONE · `cd3a5da` · 2026-07-02
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §10 reconnection/backpressure pinned by the Phase-0 API spike (L305/L307), OQ-002 resolved spike 0.5 (L408) · **Depends:** 8.5 · **Blocks:** —
**Files:** apps/worker/src/api/stream/{backpressure,resume}.ts
On reconnect the client resumes from its last acknowledged sequence; read-model changes committed during the disconnect are caught up via snapshot-or-replay, with no silently dropped committed change — resume.ts fails closed on an over-horizon gap by emitting an explicit RESYNC control frame rather than a silent partial replay. Backpressure bounds each connection's outbound buffer; on overflow the policy is explicit (coalesce read-model deltas and/or signal re-sync) — never unbounded memory growth and never a silent partial loss leaving the UI inconsistent. A slow or stalled consumer cannot block other subscribers or the worker event loop (per-connection isolation). Exact buffer bound, heartbeat interval, and resume-window thresholds are taken from the Phase-0 API spike outputs (OQ-002), not hard-coded ad hoc.

### 9.2 — Per-launch session-token mint + preload injection + authenticated worker client
- [x] DONE · `0788b1d6` · 2026-07-03

**Files:** apps/desktop/main/session-token.ts · renderer/lib/trpc.ts · extended preload/index.ts
Electron main mints a cryptographically-random per-launch token, generated fresh each launch and never persisted; it reaches the renderer ONLY via preload injection (not on window/global, not in served HTML, never logged) so other localhost clients cannot discover it. The renderer worker client attaches the token + an allowlisted Origin/Host on every tRPC call and the event-stream handshake; a missing/wrong token or disallowed Origin surfaces a typed auth-failure and does NOT silently retry an unauthenticated path.

- ⛔ **There is no per-record identity to link TO.** `AuditRepository` (`packages/db/src/repositories/interfaces.ts:555-578`) has exactly `append` + `query(filter, limit)`. **No `get(id)`, no row id** — `AuditRecord`'s header states *"Carries NO `id` (per the Appendix-A field list)."*
- ⭐ **The opaque handle already EXISTS and cannot be resolved.** `UiSafeRecentChange.changeId` (`ui-safe.ts:313-318`) is a **derived SHA-256** minted at projection time (`api/projections/recentChanges.ts:62-64`) over `workspaceId+event+occurredAt+payloadHash+refs`. ⛔ **`audit.query({ref: changeId})` will NOT work — `changeId` is never written into any record's `refs[]`.** Resolution needs a new repo capability or a re-scan-and-re-derive.
- `UiSafeEgressStatus` carries no audit ref either (three fields, defensively re-projected — `systemHealth.ts:47-51,126-132`).
⇒ **Scope = contracts (allowlist entry + the redaction decision) + worker (read path) + possibly db (resolution). Three areas and a policy call.**
⛔ **THE DECISION IS THE OWNER'S / LEAD'S, NOT THE ORCHESTRATOR'S: which `AuditRecord` fields may reach the renderer?** The record carries `actor`, `event`, `refs[]`, `payloadHash`, `beforeSummary`, `afterSummary`, `timestamps`, `workspaceId`. ⚠ **`beforeSummary`/`afterSummary` are summaries of mutations** — plausibly the most sensitive content in the operational store — and `projectRecentChanges` already drops `refs`/`payloadHash`/`actor`. A defensible answer is **`event` + `occurredAt` only**, but the existing drops are deliberate three times over, so reversing any of them is a redaction-policy call on a frozen surface. Same shape as 9.8's `UiSafeApproval` enrichment, which the lead pre-ruled comes to them.
⭐ **THE SAFE SHAPE ALREADY HAS PRECEDENT — start here, don't invent:** `globalDrillDown` (`api/procedures/queries.ts:746-751`) takes an **opaque pointer**, re-derives everything **server-side**, **re-checks scope-ownership per drill (WS-8)**, and never trusts a client-supplied ref. ⇒ a drill-down can take the existing `changeId`, resolve `auditRef` **internally**, and return a fresh narrow UI-safe summary — **`auditRef` never leaves the worker.** Still a contract change (a new summary shape needs an allowlist entry) but it **reverses no existing drop**.
⭐⭐ **PARKED AS A SHAPED ARC — LEAD RULING 2026-07-29. The redaction question is ANSWERED; whoever picks this up cold finds a scoped arc, not an open question.** ⛔ **The ruling reverses NO existing drop, which is why it is the lead's and not the owner's.**
1. **Adopt the `globalDrillDown` shape** (`api/procedures/queries.ts:746-751`): opaque `changeId` in → **server-side re-derive** → **WS-8 scope re-check PER DRILL** → never trust a client-supplied ref.
2. ⛔ **`auditRef` NEVER leaves the worker.** No new UI-safe field on `healthItem` or `recentChange`.
3. **The new narrow summary carries `event` + `occurredAt` ONLY.**
4. ⛔ **NOT `beforeSummary`/`afterSummary` — and the REASON is the ruling, not the exclusion:** the user-facing value of an audit link is **PROVENANCE** (*"this change is audited; here is when, and what kind"*), **not the mutation's contents — because the renderer ALREADY SHOWS THE CHANGE ITSELF.** So the summaries add **unbounded-raw-content risk for ZERO informational gain.** ⚠ `ui-safe.ts:310` drops them as **"unbounded raw"** — not merely *sensitive*, and that single word decides the question. **A future reader who wants them has to defeat this argument, not merely re-raise the request.**
5. **NOT `actor`, `refs[]`, `payloadHash`, or `workspaceId`** — all already deliberately dropped, and `workspaceId` on a renderer-facing type is the same WS-8 question the lead pre-ruled for 9.8's `UiSafeApproval` enrichment.
⇒ **ARC SHAPE: contracts (ONE new narrow summary entry in `UI_SAFE_ALLOWLIST`) → worker (the drill-down resolver). ⛔ NO db change** — `query(filter, limit)` plus server-side re-derivation is sufficient, **which is why `AuditRepository`'s absent row id is NOT a blocker.**
⭐ **THE EXECUTABLE STATE FOR THIS SUB-ARC NOW LIVES AT `### 9.41`, NOT HERE — 2026-07-30.** The design rationale stays in this entry (it is 9.10's, and the lead's ruling belongs beside the arc it shaped), but the **checkbox, legs, Files and Done-when moved to a first-class heading.** ⛔ **Why: this sub-arc had narrative-only state, which this file's own format contract (`:12-21`) forbids — and the cost was concrete, not cosmetic.** `spec-lint`'s Task-ID check reduces `9.10-D` to `9.10`, which resolves to **this arc's `[~]` checkbox**, so a brief citing "9.10-D" would have **linted GREEN against the wrong task**, conflating one leg with the whole arc. A false-green, produced by a rule this document states about itself.
⭐ **THE DESIGN INTENT IS ALREADY IN THE CODE — nobody built the consumer.** `deriveChangeId`'s own docstring (`api/projections/recentChanges.ts:62-64`) states it exists for a drill-down that *"re-derives server-side + re-checks scope"* and *"leaks no field verbatim."* ⇒ **the `globalDrillDown` pattern is not a new invention for this arc; it is what `changeId` was designed for.** Corroborating: `AuditRepository`'s header calls itself *"OPERATIONAL TRUTH, APPEND-ONLY"* and notes that workspace-scoped `query` **IS** *"the intended WS-8 posture."*

The get-before-upsert guard L30 mandates was implemented for `type` and never extended to the `egressPolicy` fields the SAME `upsert` overwrites; the `get` already happens for the type check, its result simply isn't used to preserve egress state. ### 9.33 — `processorOfRoute` is not total: a blank identity THROWS instead of denying (⚠ rule-5 fail-open-by-crash)
- [x] DONE · `ceb42987` · 2026-07-28 (⚠ state line reconciled 2026-07-29 — it still read OPEN while this phase's own acceptance block already listed `ceb42987` as landed; banked as the house rule the fix itself established: **a safety gate that THROWS where it should DENY hands its caller a crash instead of a denial**, now cited by the #45 constraint and by the #36 no-fix verdict)
**Kind:** fix · **Spec:** §5 (egress veto / processor identity), §16 (typed errors, never throw across a boundary) · **Depends:** — · **Blocks:** — · **Brief:** `docs/briefs/210-9.33-processor-of-route-totality.md`
**Files:** `packages/policy/src/processors.ts` · `packages/policy/test/`
`processorOfRoute` documents itself pure and fail-closed, and its malformed-route branches correctly return `processorId("MALFORMED_ROUTE")` (egress, never non-egress). **Then it brands the route's raw identity, and the brand constructor THROWS on a blank string** — so `{provider: ""}` arriving from a deserialized row throws instead of denying. The guards are exhaustive over the cases their author enumerated; **the throw lives after them.** ⚠ **Why it is rule-5 and not tidiness:** this is the identity layer directly beneath the egress veto, so a throw on an untrusted route is a **fail-open-by-crash** — the caller receives an exception rather than a deny, and whether that denies depends entirely on the caller's error handling. provint contained it at their own boundary (one `try` ⇒ deny) during task #21, which protects *that* caller and leaves **every other one exposed** — hence a task rather than a call-site fix. **Done-when:** a blank/malformed identity on either branch denies rather than throws, **no well-formed route's egress classification moves** (the no-drift pin), and the caller audit is reported. *(origin: 2026-07-28 provint task #21 flag 3; contracts L78 is this task's generalization)*

### 10.1 — Mandatory redaction layer + structured logger (non-bypassable security invariant)
- [x] DONE · `9fd682a6` · 2026-07-02
**Kind:** build · **Spec:** §16 Observability/structured-logging/redaction; REQ-S-003 (secrets/raw never logged), REQ-S-002 (Employer-Work raw never logged) · **Depends:** none · **Blocks:** 10.8
**Files:** packages/contracts/src/observability/log-record.ts; packages/domain/src/redaction/redact.ts + redaction-rules.ts; apps/worker/src/observability/logger.ts
Structured records carry correlation ID + workflowRunId (+ workspaceId where present); the logger is the SINGLE chokepoint — no path reaches a sink without first passing redaction. Redaction runs BEFORE any sink, stripping credential-shaped strings and §16 raw-content fields (provider prompts, raw Employer-Work content, AgentResult.logs), never emitted at default level; raw is reachable only behind an explicit non-default debug flag, and Employer-Work raw stays redacted even then (§5). Fail-safe by allowlist of known-safe fields (denylist insufficient) — an unclassifiable field defaults to redacted; coverage includes thrown Errors / exception messages / stack traces. ### 10.2 — Error-handling convention: typed Result + failure taxonomy + nothing-fails-silently routing
- [x] DONE · `9fd682a6` · 2026-07-02

In-flight side effects recover via Temporal resume (LIFE-3) reusing the §8 external-write envelope so an interrupted side effect is NOT duplicated (replay matches receipt/canonical key); recovery is idempotent + re-drivable, and a failure to recover surfaces a typed item rather than silently dropping the run. #### 13.8g-C — THE CODEBASE DISAGREES WITH ITSELF ABOUT WHETHER AN EXTRACTION FIELD CAN BE A LIST (the reason 13.8g-B ships INERT)

⛔ **DECIDED 2026-07-31 — LEAD RULING, owner-delegated as "the most architecturally correct answer." Direction (ii), REFINED; ⛔ do NOT implement (ii) as it was written below.** **The refinement is load-bearing: do NOT globally widen `isPrimitiveOrTbd`** — it is generic across every `ExtractionField`, so widening it admits arrays for **all** fields and flips a rule-2 surface from default-closed to default-open. ⭐ **That defect was in the ORCHESTRATOR's own framing of option (ii) and the lead caught it.** **Instead — per-field, schema-declared, default-CLOSED list support:** (1) list-ness is a property of the **FIELD's declaration in `sow:agent-extraction`**, not of the gate; an undeclared field stays scalar-only and is rejected exactly as today; (2) a declared list is **`string[]` only** — elements scalar-validated, **length-capped**, **nesting rejected**; objects/functions stay forbidden everywhere, which is what `meeting-extraction.ts:70`'s comment actually guards; (3) **TWO independent mechanisms** — Zod **and** the generated JSON Schema, so ajv holds even if the TS type is bypassed (13.18/§DEC-CANDGATE precedent; a compile-time claim over runtime-untrusted bytes is L103's inverse); (4) **contract-first sequencing** — `packages/contracts` (schema + snapshot) → worker (gate) → knowledge (⭐ the normalizer should need **NO** change; if it does, that is a **finding**); (5) **`security-reviewer` MANDATORY** on the gate slice — rule 2; (6) **delete nothing** — the three branches become live, which is the point.
⚠ **CALL IT A RELAXATION (orchestrator pushback, 2026-07-31, accepted as a correction to the ruling's framing).** The ruling described this as *"not relaxing the gate — making its prohibition precise."* **That is accurate about the MECHANISM and soft about the DIRECTION:** after this change the gate admits a value shape it previously rejected. Narrow-and-governed does not mean not-a-relaxation. ⇒ **the honest sentence is "a SCOPED, DECLARED, DEFAULT-CLOSED RELAXATION of a rule-2 gate."** **Why the word matters practically: it sets the review posture.** A reviewer told *"a prohibition was made precise"* checks the new rule is well-formed; a reviewer told *"a candidate-data gate was relaxed"* asks **what can now get through that could not before, and whether the opt-in itself can be forged** — and only the second reviewer asks whether a candidate can declare its own list-ness. On a rule-2 surface we want the second reviewer.
⛔ **RULED 2026-07-31 (lead, on orchestrator pushback — the gap was real): DECLARE BOTH `attendees` AND `decisions`.** ⭐ **And the load-bearing half is NOT which fields — it is that LIST-NESS HAS EXACTLY ONE SOURCE.** The declaration lives in one place; the gate reads it; consumers read it. ⛔ **No consumer may hand-assume via a local `Array.isArray` against its own belief — that divergence IS the bug, and re-creating it per-consumer merely relocates it.** ⭐ **Establish whether a cheap test can pin the CORRESPONDENCE — declared-as-list ⟺ consumed-as-list — and if one exists, write it: that is what prevents instance #3, and it is the make-it-unrepresentable pattern aimed at the DISAGREEMENT rather than at either half. If no cheap pin exists, SAY SO in the Step-9 flags** — *"we couldn't"* is a fine answer; an unmentioned gap is not. **State the criterion in-code so the next list-shaped field is not a judgement call.** ⛔ **ALSO RULED — the forgery question is a MANDATORY security-review item answered BY CONSTRUCTION, not by inspection: A CANDIDATE MUST NOT BE ABLE TO DECLARE ITS OWN LIST-NESS.** The schema declares; the payload never does. **Any path where model output influences which fields are treated as lists is a rule-2 BREACH and a Finding to the lead, not a design detail.** ⭐ Leg A's design answers it structurally — JSON Schema's `properties` (declared keys) over `additionalProperties` (scalar-only rest) is default-closed by precedence, and **a payload cannot add itself to `properties`**. ⛔ **HAZARD carried into leg A's brief:** `propertyNames` (the prototype-pollution guard) is emitted from `z.record`'s KEY schema, and `.object().catchall()` has no key-schema slot — the container swap can **silently drop a guard a prior security review added** (`agent-extraction.ts:40-47`). **Verify it survives by READING the regenerated JSON; if it cannot, ESCALATE rather than trading one guard for the other.**

### 24.1 — Upgrade REQ-S-NEW-008 doctor from report-only to active OS one-writer enforcement (ACL / advisory-lock)
- [~] PARTIAL · landed: `acquireSingleOwnerLock` — a real OS-atomic `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` lockfile acquire with no TOCTOU window (the `open()` syscall itself fails EEXIST), stale-pid reclaim confirmed via `process.kill(pid,0)` ESRCH, a genuinely-live pid never displaced, idempotent release — proven by SPAWNING A REAL SECOND OS PROCESS that imports the production module (not a reimplementation), every physical-refusal / stale-reclaim / live-not-reclaimed assertion mutation-verified RED; plus `resolvePgliteLockHolder` feeding `packages/knowledge`'s `evaluateWriteFence` end to end (INTACT when held, fail-closed BREACH on `pglite_lock_not_worker_held`) (`cf655c95`); remaining: ⛔ THE WRITE IS STILL NOT PHYSICALLY BLOCKED, AND THE SOURCE SAYS SO. Two real steps landed: `68ec73c9` makes `bootWorker` ACQUIRE the lock before the operational store opens (a durable `dbPath` collides on a stable path; never throws per §16 — refusal mints a `worker_down` HealthItem, code-only per rule 7), and `eed76756` registers `single_owner_lock` in `runDoctor`'s checks array over the `packages/contracts` enum widened at `7b115b02`. ⛔ BUT `boot.ts:2363-2368` records the scope in its own words: this closes the zero-production-callers gap, it does NOT bind `resolvePgliteLockHolder` → `packages/knowledge`'s `evaluateWriteFence` (measured: zero references outside its own module/tests), "so the OS lock is a real ACQUISITION but not yet the thing that would make a refused write PHYSICALLY blocked at the gbrain/vault write layer". ⚠ AND ON REFUSAL THE WORKER STILL BOOTS — the same comment states restructuring `bootWorker`'s return contract to hard-refuse serving was out of that slice's scope. ⭐ **CLOSED 2026-08-28 (`49f2b977`) — THE WRITE IS NOW PHYSICALLY BLOCKED.** The write-fence bind landed: `install/lock/writeFenceProbe.ts` builds a probe from the REAL acquire outcome, boot threads it through `ProofSpineParams.writeFence` → `KnowledgeWriterDeps`, and `atomicCommit` REFUSES with a typed `write_fence_breached` **before staging a byte** (pinned by a recording vault asserting ZERO filesystem touches). ⛔ **NOT via a hard-refuse boot contract, deliberately** — that reading is both a large breaking change to a return type with no failure variant AND the wrong layer: the fence guards WRITES, not the process lifecycle, and the lock can be LOST mid-run, so a startup decision would authorize every later write on an expired fact. The probe is therefore evaluated **PER COMMIT** (pinned: lock lost between two commits, only the second refused). A breach keeps its OWN failure code rather than folding into `commit_failed` — that code is the RETRYABLE infra route and this is permanent until an operator acts; the new member propagated through four exhaustive mappers, each compiler-surfaced. ⚠ **REMAINING, and named rather than absorbed:** `workerIsSoleVaultWriter` is a STATED fact (no filesystem-ACL prober exists) and `observedProcesses` is EMPTY (no continuous ps/lsof stray-writer sweep), so a stray write-capable gbrain process is not yet DETECTED — the LOCK half is enforced, those two are not. Recorded in the clean-install acceptance `KNOWN_GAPS`.

1. **CONCEPT-LEVEL enumeration, never known string forms.** The orchestrator's own design-doc sweep needed THREE iterations because the first grepped the phrasings already known — 4 of 9 sites found. **A string-shaped audit returns a confident false all-clear, which is worse than not running it** (contracts L64). Report the search KEY and the dry-iteration count.
2. **BOTH mechanisms.** Asserted-constant (a claim stated from a constant/default-seed) AND **fail-open-by-omission** (a claim implied by a MISSING element — e.g. a warning that renders only when data is present, so "no data" and "nothing to warn about" look identical). They look nothing alike in code and a sweep tuned to one will miss the other.
3. **DOCS AND DESIGN AUTHORITY IN SCOPE, not just code.** The chrome pill's mandate lived in a locked screen-GENERATION prompt and in a normative governance principle — **a code-only audit would have cleared it** while the generator kept reproducing the defect.
4. **The question is "is this claim DERIVED from the state that governs it, at the SCOPE that state applies to" — NOT "is this claim currently true."**
5. **TEST ASSERTIONS AND FAKES ARE IN SCOPE** (added 2026-07-26 from the headline finding above). A safety claim can be defended by a test that pins it, or normalized by a fake that models it — neither appears in production code. Sweep assertions and fixtures with the same concept-level method, and treat a test asserting a safety value as a claim requiring the same derivation check as the code. A claim that happens to be true today but cannot move when the governing state moves is a decoration that reads as a guarantee.
**Scoping note (orchestrator's call, 2026-07-26):** deliberately NOT ridden on the Phase-9 exit. ### 24.19 — The "key-name-independent, recursive" raw-content gate does not traverse every container shape it claims to cover (24.6 round-3 finding WS-1/F15 — rule 4)
- [x] DONE `4cef394f` 2026-08-11 (knowledge) · **Depends:** — · **Blocks:** —
**Kind:** fix · **Spec:** §5, §6 · **Safety rule 4** · **Files:** `packages/contracts/src/models/gcl-projection.ts:37-51` (`isRawContentShaped`/`carriesRawContent`) · `packages/contracts/schemas/gcl-projection.schema.json:21-24` · `packages/contracts/test/models/gcl-projection.test.ts`
**THE CLAIM (in-code, `:23-26`):** *"the gate is KEY-NAME-INDEPENDENT: it scans EVERY value recursively (nested objects + arrays) and rejects any string that is multi-line OR exceeds the summary length cap, regardless of key name."*
⛔ **FALSE FOR TWO CONTAINER SHAPES.** The traversal is `Array.isArray` → recurse, else `typeof === "object"` → recurse over **`Object.entries(value)`**, which enumerates only **own enumerable string-keyed** properties. Both of these are `typeof === "object"` yet yield `[]`, so the function falls through to *"not raw-content-shaped"* **without inspecting their contents**: (1) **`Map`/`Set`** — `Object.entries(new Map([["x","…multi-line raw…"]]))` → `[]`; (2) **non-enumerable own properties** via `Object.defineProperty(…, {enumerable:false})`.
⛔ **AND THERE IS NO AJV BACKSTOP:** the generated schema has `sanitizedPayload.additionalProperties: {}` — **unconstrained** — so **the Zod `.refine` is the ONLY enforcement, not defence-in-depth over a schema floor.** (Read from the emitted file, not inferred.)
⚠ **Nested arrays, objects-in-arrays and deep nesting ARE handled correctly** — confirmed against the module's own adversarial tests, **which stop exactly there.** `Array.prototype.some`'s short-circuit is correct, not a bypass.
⭐ **No end-to-end leak found in currently-wired code** (no producer builds such a payload; the one concrete `sanitizedPayload` consumer filters to `string|number|boolean` and would drop a `Map` — **fail-safe by accident, not by design**). ⛔ **The finding is that the code's own STATED GUARANTEE is false for these shapes and nothing tests the boundary.**
**Done-when:** either `sanitizedPayload`'s runtime shape is structurally restricted to what `Object.entries`/`JSON.parse` can produce (a non-plain-object/array value is its own rejection reason — cheap and structural, the preferred fix), **or** the traversal iterates `Reflect.ownKeys` plus `Map`/`Set`; **and adversarial tests exist for both shapes.** ⚠ **Carried-forward unknown, do not assume it away:** whether the concrete `GclProjectionRepository` adapters silently drop a `Map` on JSON serialization was **not verified.** *(origin: 2026-08-11, 24.6 round 3, WS-1)*

### 24.52 — Once a real `GclAuditPersistPort` binds, `crossWorkspaceRead`'s per-row loop issues N SERIAL awaited audit writes with no cap — unbounded latency and unbounded audit-store growth

Pins, each RED-verified by reverting to the naive unbounded pass-through: wall-time independent of N controlled-delay writes (settles via microtasks alone, fake timers never advanced), a never-resolving port never blocks completion, and the queue-full / per-write-timeout drop accounting. Byte-equivalent on today's unbound path ⇒ the bound is in place BEFORE any real port binds, which is what made this a precondition. ⛔ **THE PHASE-25.2/25.4 PORT-BINDING PRECONDITION IS HEREBY DISCHARGED.** · filed 2026-08-12 (found by `security-reviewer`) · **Depends:** `24.44` · **Track:** knowledge + worker (composition root)
**Kind:** fix (safety/robustness) · **Spec:** §5, §16 · Safety rule 4 · **Files:** `apps/worker/src/composition/crossWorkspaceRead.ts` (the per-link row loop) · `packages/knowledge/src/gcl/projection.ts` (`persistDenialAudit`)
⛔ **THE FINDING:** `resolveApprovedCrossWorkspaceSlice` loops per row and now `await`s `serveProjection`, which `await`s `persistDenialAudit` on every denial. **With a real port bound, N denied rows ⇒ N SERIAL awaited audit writes inside a read path, with no cap and no batching** — a latency surface on a cross-workspace read and an unbounded-growth surface on the audit store. **A hostile or merely large tampered set turns one read into N writes.**
⭐ **`24.44`'s own shape one layer out — the defect ARRIVES WITH THE BINDING**, exactly as `24.50` arrives with `24.15`'s fix and `24.45` arrives with its own. ⚠ **Not fixable in `24.44`: the port is unbound, so there is nothing to bound yet** — which is precisely why it must gate the binding rather than trail it (`L106`: safe-by-dormancy is not a guarantee).

```sh
awk '/^## Phase 24 /,/^## Phase 25 /' /tmp/h_plan.txt > /tmp/h_sec.txt     # 593 lines
awk '/\*\*Spec:\*\*/' /tmp/h_sec.txt > /tmp/h_spec.txt                     # 54 lines
grep -o '§[0-9][0-9.]*' /tmp/h_spec.txt > /tmp/h_tok.txt                   # 81 = TOTAL
sort -u /tmp/h_tok.txt | wc -l                                             # 16 = DISTINCT
sort /tmp/h_tok.txt | uniq -c | sort -rn > /tmp/h_freq.txt
awk '{s+=$1} END{print s}' /tmp/h_freq.txt                                 # 81 — sum control
```
⭐ **THREE CONTROLS, chosen because this task itself proves one control is not enough:** (1) **non-vacuity** — `§16` counted independently = 23 ✓; (2) **anti-truncation** — freq-table ROWS (16) == `sort -u` DISTINCT (16), the check this task prescribes after the `head -12` incident ✓; (3) **sum** — table counts total 81 == occurrence count 81 ✓.
⛔⛔ **THE CONFLATION THIS RESOLVES, AND IT IS THE REUSABLE PART: TWO DIFFERENT NUMBERS WERE IN PLAY AND ONLY ONE WAS EVER TRUNCATED.** The `head -12` defect (recorded below) hit the **CLASSIFIER-CORRECTED** count — `77` vs `76`. It never touched the **RAW** `16/81` extraction, which came through a different command. ⇒ **"my count came through a pipe, so it may be truncated" is a hypothesis about a SPECIFIC command, not a property of every number in the vicinity** — and re-testing the wrong one would have "confirmed" a figure nobody doubted while leaving the doubted one unmeasured.

⚠ **RESIDUAL IN THE LEAD'S CORRECTED LIST, reconciled here rather than inherited:** their corrected undeclared set names **six** anchors (`§16`·`§5`·`§8`·`§11`·`§9`·`§12`, 50 citations), but **`5 declared + 6 undeclared = 11`, not 12.** The missing member is **`§19.13`** (1 citation) — a REAL anchor under the classifier (`§19.x` is real), NOT in Phase 24's declared set, and in fact **Phase 26's anchor.** ⇒ **the undeclared set is SEVEN anchors / 51 citations:** `§16`23 · `§5`14 · `§8`8 · `§11`3 · `§9`1 · `§19.13`1 · `§12`1. **`5 + 7 = 12` ✓.** ⛔ **Whoever runs this slice re-derives all of it and states which classifier they used — the number is not the deliverable, the classifier decision is.**
⛔⛔⛔ **THREE MEASUREMENTS OF THE SAME 572 LINES, THREE DIFFERENT SETS, AND — THE FINDING — THREE DIFFERENT FAILURE MECHANISMS. NO SINGLE CONTROL WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ALL THREE.** *(confirmed by the lead 2026-08-13; all three attempts were theirs or the orchestrator's, none was a tooling defect the other party could have flagged)*
> 1. **FABRICATION** — the intercepted `grep` returned memory-search results on a zero-hit query ⇒ the orchestrator's **"13"** (real: 23). **Caught by re-running under a different tool.**
> 2. **TRUNCATION** — a sorted frequency list piped through `head -12` silently dropped its tail ⇒ the lead's **77** and their `§13.6`-in/`§12`-out set. **A non-vacuity control would have PASSED here** — every printed row's count was correct.

> 4. ⭐ **CUMULATIVE COUNTER** *(added 2026-08-13, worker-implementer, self-caught during `24.58`'s enumeration)* — `find … | xargs awk` leaves **`NR` cumulative ACROSS files**, so **filenames are correct while every line number is garbage.** ⛔ **Like transcription, it produces confidently PRECISE wrong output — the most quotable failure shape there is.** **Fix: `FNR`, not `NR`.** ⚠ **A reader has no way to tell these line numbers from good ones**, which is why it is recorded here rather than left as a footnote in one slice.
> ⇒ ⭐⭐ ***The classifier — and the enumeration itself — is the deliverable, not the number.*** **Three competent attempts, three mechanisms, and the only thing that caught each was a DIFFERENT party re-deriving it.** ⚠ **Mechanism 3 is the one no command-level control reaches at all**: the fix is to derive the dependent list (declared / undeclared) **from the extraction**, never to hand-assemble it alongside.
⛔⛔ **TWO of those failure modes have DIFFERENT CONTROLS — and knowing one gave NO protection against the other (lead's own finding against their own rule).** The `grep`-interception note below prescribes a **non-vacuity control** (run a term known to be present; a sensible count proves the search read the file). ⚠ **That control addresses FABRICATION and is USELESS against TRUNCATION** — a `head`-ed frequency list returns perfectly sensible counts for every row it prints while silently dropping the tail, so a control term would have passed happily. ⇒ **the check that catches truncation is different: compare `sort -u | wc -l` against the number of rows actually printed, or simply NEVER `head` a frequency list you intend to draw a TOTAL from.** ⭐ ***Two mechanisms, two controls; the person who prescribed the first was caught by the second.***
⭐ **RULING (lead, 2026-08-13) — option 3 REFINED: do not delete the check; TYPE the phase.** **A subset check is not mis-parameterized on Phase 24 — it is CATEGORICALLY INAPPLICABLE.** A hardening finding cites whatever spec section the defect happens to live in; **that set is unpredictable in advance and unbounded by design**, so asserting `brief ⊆ phase` against it asserts something that cannot be true. ⇒ **Declare Phase 24's KIND explicitly (cross-cutting hardening; anchor set OPEN by construction) and have `spec-lint` skip the SUBSET assertion for phases so marked — while STILL requiring every brief to declare its own anchors.** The per-brief declaration is the half that carries information (it tells a reader where the work lands); the subset assertion is the half that cannot hold. **Keep the first, drop only the second, and only for phases that declare themselves open.**
⛔ **TWO OPTIONS RULED OUT, WITH THEIR REASONS — recorded so nobody re-proposes them when the lint noise returns:**

> **BLIND SPOT B — CONSTRUCTIONS, NOT ASSERTIONS** *(found verifying `#69`)*: making a `WriteSuccess` field required enumerated **2** sites; **`as WriteSuccess` appears 12 times across four further files**, incl. `as unknown as WriteSuccess`. **`as T` is permitted because `T` is assignable to the literal's inferred type — the missing property is never checked.**
> ⚠ **Two blind spots found HOURS APART, both by implementers, both against the orchestrator's recommendation — which the lead also endorsed.** ⇒ **it cannot be offered as the sound substitute for the three broken tools.**
⭐⭐⭐ **AND THE ROUND'S ACTUAL FINDING IS THE SHAPE ALL FOUR SHARE, NOT THE FAILURES: `contracts L178` — a NON-VACUITY control asks *did the instrument RUN?*, an APPLICABILITY control asks *is it VALID FOR THIS INPUT?*, and a non-vacuity control passes happily on an inapplicable instrument.** ⛔ **THREE instances in two days — `L177` (a wired consumer answering the wrong question), the whitespace-normalising comparison (valid until the data contains whitespace), and the compiler here.** ⇒ ***the first three entries are instruments FAILING and are the noisy part; entry 4 is an instrument WORKING on a question it cannot answer, and nothing in its output says so.*** ⚠ **`contracts L179` is the operational half: when two methods disagree, EXPLAIN the delta rather than picking a winner — here the name-keyed census was the MORE complete one and was retracted in favour of the compiler.**
⛔⛔ **BUT THE SUBSTITUTE HAS ITS OWN TRUNCATION, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE USABLE PART (knowledge-implementer, `#78`): THE INSTRUMENT IS SOUND; THE INVOCATION TRUNCATES.** `turbo` **halts dependents on the first failure**, so a single forced run **under-reports the surface** — observed as `Tasks: 14 successful, 16 total`, and separately as `14 successful + 1 named failure` failing to sum to `16` because the summary names only the FIRST failure. ⇒ ***a compiler-derived enumeration is complete ONLY if re-derived PER-PACKAGE***; run repo-wide through a halting task-runner it is a property-based enumeration **delivered through a truncating pipe**. ⭐ **That is the same shape as `L155`'s pipe — and it is worth separating carefully, because "the compiler cannot be forged" is TRUE and does not mean "this run saw everything."** ⚠ **Pair it with the arithmetic check: if successes + named failures ≠ total, the list is truncated and you have not seen the surface.**
⛔⛔ **TWO SUBSTANTIVE BOUNDS FOUND THE SAME DAY, BOTH BY IMPLEMENTERS, BOTH AGAINST THE ORCHESTRATOR'S RECOMMENDATION — AND TOGETHER THEY SAY THE COMPILER ANSWERS A NARROWER QUESTION THAN WE WERE ASKING OF IT.**
> **BOUND 1 — IT COVERS THE MAPPERS, NOT THE CONSUMERS** *(worker, `### 24.85` / `#83`)*. `hermesAutomation.ts:617` hardcodes `advance(state, [… "write_conflict"])` for every commit failure and **never switches on the code**, so widening the union surfaced nothing there. ⇒ **a consumer that HARDCODES is invisible to an exhaustiveness guard.**
> **BOUND 2 — IT COVERS ASSIGNMENT-CHECKED CONSTRUCTIONS, NOT CASTS** *(found while verifying `#69`)*. Making a `WriteSuccess` field required enumerated **2** sites; **`as WriteSuccess` appears 12 times across FOUR further files**, including `as unknown as WriteSuccess`. ⭐ **`as T` is an ASSERTION — TS permits it because `T` is assignable to the literal's inferred type, so the missing property is never checked.** ⇒ ***"required is free" was TRUE AND MISLEADING: nothing broke precisely BECAUSE the casts hid the constructions***, and the field would have been required in the type and absent in practice.
⭐⭐ **AND THE PROCESS LESSON IS SHARPER THAN EITHER BOUND: the orchestrator instructed an implementer to REPLACE a name-keyed census with the compiler enumeration, and the name-keyed census had been MORE COMPLETE.** ⇒ ***NEITHER METHOD DOMINATES — the symbol search over-includes mentions, the compiler under-includes casts and hardcoding consumers, and THE UNION is what you want.*** ⛔ **Recommending one as a replacement for the other is the defect; recommending it as a SECOND SURFACE is the fix** (`contracts L178` — and note the compiler is a genuinely better instrument than the three above, which is exactly why its narrowness is easy to miss).
⚠ **BOUNDARY, STATED SO THIS IS NOT READ AS AN ALL-CLEAR (`L100`): counts reported in THIS session went through redirect-then-measure with positive and negative controls. Grep-derived claims committed in EARLIER sessions are UNAUDITED, and a sweep of them is NOT scheduled** — the lead ruled against a parallel audit in favour of `### 24.6`'s residual block, whose triggered rule fires on open work only.
**Done-when:** the three failure modes and the hit-vs-empty asymmetry are stated where agents are told to prefer these tools (root `CLAUDE.md` + the area guides' code-intelligence notes), so the instruction and its known failure modes travel together. *(origin: 2026-08-14, orchestrator + worker + providers, independently)*

### 24.89 — `MdContentShaSchema`'s `/i` flag is DROPPED when the JSON Schema is emitted, so ajv is STRICTER than Zod for the same field

- [x] DONE · `65979e61` · 2026-08-25 (the `/i` drop itself rode in `27640ebe`'s `zod-brands.ts` hunk; this commit PINS it) · filed 2026-08-17 (main-orchestrator; **found by contract-implementer while measuring `### 24.84`'s snapshot blast radius — adjacent, pre-existing, and flagged rather than absorbed**) · **Depends:** — · **Blocks:** — · **Track:** contract (`packages/contracts`)
**Kind:** fix · **Spec:** §3, §16 · **Files:** `packages/contracts/src/primitives/` (`MdContentShaSchema`) · its generated `*.schema.json`
⛔ **THE DEFECT:** the Zod source is `/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i` — **case-insensitive** — but the emitted JSON Schema is `"^[0-9a-f]{64}$"`, **with the `i` flag silently dropped.** ⇒ ***an uppercase-hex sha PASSES the Zod gate and FAILS the ajv gate for the same value.*** **The two validators disagree on the same field, and the emitted artifact is the frozen one.**
⭐ **WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS FIELD, and why it is filed rather than fixed in passing:** this is a **generator fidelity** gap, not a one-field typo — **any regex brand carrying a flag is exposed the same way**, and the JSON-Schema emitter is the surface the candidate-data gate (REQ-S-006) runs on. ⚠ **Whether other flag-bearing regexes exist is UNMEASURED — do not assume this is the only one; enumerate before fixing** (`L100`, and the `### 24.46` class: a predicate can be perfectly single-sourced and still be wrong).
⭐ **PROVENANCE WORTH KEEPING: it was found because `### 24.84`'s proposed shape was deliberately FLAG-FREE so it would round-trip faithfully** — the author checked whether their own regex survived emission, and the check surfaced a neighbour's that does not. **A fidelity check run on one's own work found a defect in someone else's.**
**Done-when:** the emitted schema and the Zod source accept the same set for `MdContentShaSchema`, **or** the divergence is documented in-file with what it costs (`L82`); and the population of flag-bearing regex brands is **enumerated with its method and boundary**, not assumed to be one. *(origin: 2026-08-17, `### 24.84` contracts leg Step 2.5)*

⚠ **AND THE NINE DO NOT AGREE ABOUT WHAT THEY ENCODE, so "just share a type" is not the safe default:** `meetingCloseout`/`projectSync`/`dailyBrief` cite **inv-5** (keyed on `idempotencyKey`); `deletionSaga.ts:256` cites **inv-4** (keyed on *"the same plan key"*); `retentionPrune` sits under **RET-3**; `crossCalendarScheduling`/`periodReview` cite **nothing**. ⛔ **A single shared type would silently collapse inv-4 and inv-5.** ⚠ **`broker.ts:209` is a DIFFERENT FACT and is excluded by construction** — unifying it in would be a bug.
⛔⛔ **RE-VERIFIED THE `### 24.88` CENSUS, INDEPENDENTLY AND POSITIVE-CONTROLLED — THE NUMBERS HOLD.** A repo-wide non-test scan (`/usr/bin/grep -rn "\.replayed\b"` over every `.ts` file outside `test/`/`*.test.ts`, the REAL binary — the session's `grep` is a `ugrep`-backed shell-function wrapper, bypassed by full path) returns **exactly ONE production property-read of `.replayed` in the whole repo: `packages/workflows/src/activities/commitKnowledge.ts:169`** (`replayed: result.value.replayed`) — a COPY into a freshly-constructed literal, never a branch (no `if`/`?:`/`&&`/`.filter` anywhere reads it, confirmed by the same scan). **Positive control:** the identical instrument found real `replayed` assignments in `writer.ts`, `tombstone.ts`, `broker.ts` and the one copy site — it demonstrably surfaces real matches, so the zero-branch result is a genuine absence, not a broken search.

⭐ **PRODUCERS — ALL REAL, NONE SYNTHESIZED.** Of the ten declared sites, only **three files anywhere in the repo actually assign a `replayed:` literal**; the other seven ("`meetingCloseout`/`projectSync`/`dailyBrief`/`crossCalendarScheduling`/`deletionSaga`/`retentionPrune`/`periodReview`") are pure port-interface declarations with zero local construction. `writer.ts:493-501` (`applyPlan`) and `tombstone.ts:249-258` (`applyTombstone`) both derive it from `deps.revisions.getByIdempotencyKey(...)` — a real `KnowledgeRevisionStore` lookup, never a hardcoded/synthesized value. `broker.ts:251-253` (`runJob`) derives it from `deps.ledger?.get(job.idempotencyKey)` — the broker's OWN ledger, a genuinely different fact, correctly excluded from the "must-agree" family by `### 24.88`. Nothing in this family is fabricated.

⛔⛔ **THE FINDING THAT ANSWERS THE "REDUNDANT?" QUESTION — `revisionId` IS CONTENT-ADDRESSED (`computeRevisionId(committedProjected)`, `writer.ts:641`), SO IT CANNOT STAND IN AS PROOF OF NON-DUPLICATION.** Two independent, genuinely non-replayed commits of byte-identical content would produce the SAME `revisionId` even if the idempotency short-circuit never fired once — a full second write that happens to hash-match is, on `revisionId` alone, indistinguishable from a true zero-write replay. ⇒ ***`replayed` is not a redundant convenience sitting beside `revisionId` — it is the ONLY field in any of these return values that distinguishes "no second write occurred" from "a second write occurred and happened to reproduce the same content."*** This is precisely safety rule 3's "no duplicate writes," applied to the Markdown-write side rather than the Tool Gateway's external-write side (ARCHITECTURE.md:169 already cites this exact `KnowledgeRevisionStore` replay path as "rule 3/inv-D" — a second, independent instantiation of the same invariant family, not a substitute for the Tool Gateway's own `{status:"created"|"reused"}` discriminator, which covers external writes only).

⭐ **AND IT IS ALREADY THAT PROOF-INSTRUMENT, ACTIVELY, TODAY — six test files with real assertions, not scaffolding literals:** `packages/knowledge/test/writer.test.ts:126,304,476` + `packages/knowledge/test/tombstone.test.ts:84,157` (unit-prove the two real producers) · `packages/providers/test/broker.test.ts:155,316` (the broker's own fact) · `packages/workflows/test/meeting-activities.test.ts:784,804` (activity-boundary pass-through) · `packages/workflows/test/meeting-fakes.test.ts:243,256` (fake-port meta-test). **Decisively: `apps/worker/test/composition/realSourceCommit.test.ts:161,189,204`** — a REAL, WIRED, end-to-end integration test over `assembleBackends`'s actual DB-backed `KnowledgeRevisionStore` that closes the worker process and reopens a fresh one over the SAME db file, asserting `c2.value.replayed === true` to prove the durable idempotency invariant SURVIVES A RESTART. Delete the field and this test — and the five others — lose the one thing they read to state what they exist to prove; per the content-addressing finding above, `revisionId` equality alone would not be an adequate substitute without building a NEW instrument (e.g. a write-count spy) that does not exist today.

⚠ **THE SIX ZERO-READ PORTS STAY ZERO — RE-CONFIRMED, POSITIVE-CONTROLLED.** A targeted search for `expect(...replayed...)` and `.replayed` across each family's own test/fakes file (`cross-calendar-scheduling.test.ts`, `deletion-saga.test.ts`, `retention-prune.test.ts`, `daily-brief-fakes.ts`, `project-sync-fakes.ts`, `period-review-fakes.ts`) returns empty for all six — they construct the field only to satisfy the TS shape, never read it. Matches `### 24.88` exactly.

⭐ **ORIGIN — `/usr/bin/git log -S "readonly replayed: boolean" --oneline --reverse -- packages/knowledge/src/knowledge-writer/writer.ts` → ONE commit, `aecb8f1e` (2026-07-01, "Phase 4 §6 — KnowledgeWriter sole-writer"), whose own message lists the build order as "composed candidate-data gate → atomic commit → compare-revision → IDEMPOTENT REPLAY → exactly-one revision/audit."** `replayed` is the founding commit's own name for the observable half of "idempotent replay" — built the same day as the mechanism it reports on, not bolted on later. `/usr/bin/git log -S replayed --oneline` shows 60 touches across the repo's 1675-commit history, one per later phase that added an output workflow — copy-paste propagation of a real, deliberate pattern, consistent with (not contradicting) `### 24.88`'s "ten independent re-declarations."

⚠ **CITATION DRIFT NOTED, NOT FIXED (out of this entry's territory):** this entry's own Blocks line names `### 24.82` and `### 24.84` — as CURRENTLY written, neither is about `replayed` (`24.82` closed on non-enumerable-property/lesson-correction residuals; `24.84` is the unrelated `WorkspaceIdSchema` write-boundary validator). Whoever re-scopes dependent tasks per the Done-when below should first confirm those two back-references are still live, since their present content has nothing left for this decision to unblock.

⛔ **THE DECISIVE QUESTION, ANSWERED: if `replayed` vanished tomorrow, the KnowledgeWriter/tombstone "idempotent replay ⇒ exactly-one revision, zero second write" invariant becomes UNPROVABLE by every test that currently proves it — six files, ~15 assertions, including the one real restart-simulating integration test — without first building a replacement instrument that does not exist today and would just reinvent this field under another name.**

⭐⭐ **RECOMMENDATION: KEEP `replayed` AS-IS.** Do not wire a new production consumer (`### 24.80`'s "add an eleventh signal to a zero-consumer family" premise stays refuted, per `### 24.88`). Do not delete or unify it (sole proof-instrument for a safety-adjacent invariant; `revisionId` cannot substitute given content-addressing).
