**Done-when:** either a **named production consumer** exists (a caller that BRANCHES on the value, not one that copies it) and is tracked as a real task, **or** it is recorded that the fact is not wanted and the family's disposition follows from that — with the decision stated once, in one place, and the four dependent tasks re-scoped against it rather than each inheriting the assumption. ⛔ **DISCHARGED ON THE SECOND BRANCH, WITH A CORRECTION THE ORIGINAL WORDING DIDN'T ANTICIPATE: no NEW production consumer is wanted, but "not wanted as a consumer" is NOT "safe to delete" — the field survives as the sole proof-instrument named above.** The re-scope of `### 24.80`/`24.82`/`24.84`/`24.88` against this decision is owed but is NOT this entry's territory (`IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` 24.90 only, per this investigation's charter). *(origin: 2026-08-17, `### 24.88` census; closed 2026-08-25)*

⭐⭐ **IT IS ANSWERABLE, AND THE REASON IS BETTER THAN "you could grep the vault": THE VAULT'S CONTENTS ARE ALREADY FILTERED BY THE WEAK PREDICATE, BY CONSTRUCTION.** `scanForSecrets` **REJECTS THE WHOLE COMMIT** on a match ⇒ **anything the KnowledgeWriter successfully wrote PASSED policy's predicate** ⇒ ***re-scanning vault content with `@sow/domain`'s correct predicate yields EXACTLY the population that would have been refused had the predicate been right.*** **No differential is needed — the filtering already happened at write time.**

- **(A) OVER-reports — the vault is HUMAN-EDITABLE.** It is an Obsidian-compatible Markdown tree; **a human pasting a credential into a note never passes through `scanForSecrets` at all** ⇒ **a hit is NOT proof the drift admitted it.** Attribution needs the vault's own history or `AuditRecord` provenance to show the write came from KnowledgeWriter. ⚠ **MOOT AT THE DEFAULT LOCATION (lead, 2026-08-18): an EMPTY tree has no human edits either** ⇒ **(A) returns ONLY if `SOW_VAULT_ROOT` was pointed at a real Obsidian vault**, which is exactly the narrowed question above.

### 24.112 — ⛔⛔ A TRAP, NOT A TIDY-UP: copying `### 24.102`'s sink redaction into `egressCommands.ts` makes a LANDED employer-egress REVOKE report FAILURE — a rule-5 regression that looks like consistency

- [x] DONE · `a284b2ad` · 2026-08-25 · filed 2026-08-18 (main-orchestrator #3, from `### 24.102` Step 9; ⭐ **found by `security-reviewer`, traced by worker-implementer, who correctly did NOT file it themselves and did NOT bake a task number into the source**) · **Depends:** `### 24.102` (creates the asymmetry) · **Blocks:** — · **Track:** worker (`apps/worker`)
**Kind:** finding (+ fix, design call) · **Spec:** §5, §10, §16 · ⛔⛔ **Safety: rule 5 — the fail-safe OFF control for employer raw egress** · **Files:** `apps/worker/src/api/procedures/egressCommands.ts` (`toUiSafeEgressStatus`, `~:90-96`), `apps/worker/src/api/procedures/egressRevoke.ts` (`~:51`), consumer `apps/desktop/renderer/lib/egress-status.ts` (`foldStatus`), surface `apps/desktop/renderer/surfaces/workspace-settings/egress.tsx` (`~:148`)
⛔ **THE SETUP:** `egressCommands.ts` defines its **own** `toUiSafeEgressStatus` — same name, same type, **returns `workspaceId` VERBATIM** — whose docblock claims to mirror the read-path projector. `### 24.102` redacted the READ path and **deliberately did not touch this one.** ⇒ **the obvious follow-up is *"make them consistent."***
⛔⛔ **THE TRAP, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS A TASK RATHER THAN A CLEANUP: `foldStatus` IS SHARED BY BOTH CALLERS AND FAILS CLOSED ON A REQUEST/RESPONSE MISMATCH.** On the READ path that renders *"posture unavailable"* — correct, and priced (`### 24.108`). **On the WRITE/REVOKE path the SAME divergence renders, verbatim at `egress.tsx:~148`: *"Couldn't revoke the acknowledgment for {label}. The posture on screen is UNCHANGED."*** ⇒ ⭐⭐ ***A REVOKE THAT ACTUALLY LANDED REPORTS FAILURE — INDISTINGUISHABLY FROM A REAL FAILURE — ON THE EMERGENCY EGRESS-OFF CONTROL.*** ⛔ **The operator's correct response to that message is to try again or to believe employer raw egress is still ON when it is OFF.**
⛔ **IT IS SAFE TODAY ONLY BECAUSE THE SIBLING IS UN-REDACTED.** ⇒ ***the asymmetry is load-bearing, and "consistency" is the exact edit that breaks it.*** ⚠ **`### 24.102`'s docblock now names this sibling BY SYMBOL and is branch-qualified to its own producer** — the type-level phrasing it previously carried was itself the mechanism by which this sibling stays invisible (`L161`: overstating a guarantee invites the reader to stop checking).
⭐ **WHY IT NEEDS A DESIGN CALL, NOT A PATCH:** the read path wants the value redacted and the write path needs the returned id to MATCH the request for its own fail-closed compare. **Those two requirements are in genuine tension on a shared consumer, and picking either one silently is how this becomes a rule-5 incident.** ⛔ **Do NOT resolve it by weakening `foldStatus`'s compare** — that check is a real WS-8-adjacent guard (`L55`).
⛔⛔ **AND THE DIRECTION IS NOT THE HAZARD — THE INDISTINGUISHABILITY IS (lead ruling 2026-08-18; the filer rated the urgency right and UNDER-rated the finding).** A landed revoke reporting failure makes the operator believe egress is **more** dangerous than it is — the conservative direction, and they retry. ⭐⭐ **The real hazard is second-order: *IT IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A REAL FAILURE* ⇒ it trains an operator that *"couldn't revoke"* sometimes means *"it actually worked"* — AND THE NEXT TIME THE CONTROL GENUINELY FAILS, THAT LESSON IS EXACTLY WRONG.** ⛔ ***A safety control that cries wolf conservatively still degrades the response to the real event.*** ⚠ **Stated because *"it fails safe"* will otherwise be read as *"it is harmless."***

#### ⛔ FENCE TEXT — SOURCE COMMENTS AT BOTH SITES (lead ruling: a tracker entry does NOT do this job)
⭐ **The hazard is a future *"make them consistent"* cleanup, and that person is reading `egressCommands.ts` and `systemHealth.ts` — NOT this file.** ⚠ **Write it so it survives being RIGHT: `secret-scan.ts`'s comment was TRUE and still misled, because it reasoned about the wrong layer** ⇒ **name WHICH TWO PRODUCERS and WHAT `foldStatus` COMPARES — never *"these are intentionally different."*** **Each site names the other by symbol. Queued as worker's next slice; text authored here so it survives the round.**
> **At `egressCommands.ts`'s `toUiSafeEgressStatus`:** *"⛔ THIS PRODUCER DELIBERATELY DOES NOT REDACT `workspaceId`, AND THE ASYMMETRY WITH `systemHealth.ts`'s SAME-NAMED `toUiSafeEgressStatus` IS LOAD-BEARING — DO NOT 'MAKE THEM CONSISTENT' (`### 24.112`). Both results are folded by ONE shared consumer, `foldStatus` (`apps/desktop/renderer/lib/egress-status.ts`), which COMPARES THE RETURNED `workspaceId` AGAINST THE REQUESTED ONE and fails closed on a mismatch. On the READ path a mismatch renders 'posture unavailable' — correct, and priced. On THIS path — the revoke — it renders 'Couldn't revoke the acknowledgment … the posture on screen is UNCHANGED', so a revoke that ACTUALLY LANDED would report failure, indistinguishably from a real failure, on the fail-safe OFF control for employer raw egress (safety rule 5). Redacting here without resolving that is a rule-5 regression that looks like a cleanup."*
> **At `systemHealth.ts`'s `toUiSafeEgressStatus`:** *"⛔ THE REDACTION HERE IS A PROPERTY OF THIS PRODUCER, NOT OF `UiSafeEgressStatus` — `egressCommands.ts` defines its own same-named projector that returns `workspaceId` VERBATIM, and that difference is deliberate (`### 24.112`). Do not propagate this gate there without reading that entry: the shared consumer `foldStatus` compares returned-vs-requested and fails closed, and on the revoke path that turns a LANDED revoke into a reported failure."*

⚠ **TWO ARTIFACT FLAGS FROM THE FENCE SLICE, RECORDED NOT FIXED (worker-implementer, 2026-08-18, correctly scoped OUT of a fence-and-only-the-fence slice):**
**(1) `egressCommands.ts`'s EXISTING docblock undercuts the fence and is read FIRST:** *"defense-in-depth — mirrors `systemHealth.ts`'s `toUiSafeEgressStatus`…"*. ⭐ **The trailing clause scopes *"mirrors"* to FIELD allowlisting, so it is NOT false** — ⛔ **but the bare verb sits three lines above a fence whose entire point is that the two deliberately DO NOT mirror.** ⚠ **Decision 2 of that slice makes this WORSE, not better: `//` comments are suppressed in TypeScript quick info while JSDoc is not, so on hover this docblock is what a reader sees.** ⇒ *the sentence that surfaces contradicts the guard that does not.*
**(2) QUOTATION PROVENANCE, so a future verifier does not mis-conclude the fence is stale:** the fence's fragment *"the posture on screen is UNCHANGED"* matches the **in-code comment at `egress.tsx:152`**, NOT the user-visible literal at `:148`, which reads *"The posture is unchanged — try again."* ⭐ **Same claim, two sentence sources.** ⛔ **Recorded ONLY so someone grepping the exact phrase lands at `:152` and does not read the fence as citing a string that no longer exists** — `L152`'s class, pre-empted rather than discovered.
**Done-when:** the tension is resolved EXPLICITLY with the chosen option's cost stated — the revoke path never reports failure for a write that landed, **and** no un-redacted `workspaceId` reaches a rule-7 sink; ⛔ **a pin exists that reds if a landed revoke reports failure**, because nothing today would catch it; ⛔ **and the in-source note is retained or superseded, never deleted** — it is the only artifact that names this trap (`L194`). *(origin: 2026-08-18, `### 24.102` Step 9, `security-reviewer` via worker-implementer)*

### 24.114 — Per-ref LENGTH is unbounded on the audit signal: cardinality is capped, individual ref length is not, so a cut failure degrades to a FULL leak rather than truncation

- [x] DONE · `3989ccc3` · 2026-08-25 · filed 2026-08-18 (main-orchestrator #3, from `### 24.103` Step 9; **knowledge-implementer, defence-in-depth**) · **Depends:** `### 24.103` · **Blocks:** — · **Track:** knowledge (`packages/knowledge`)
**Kind:** fix (defence-in-depth) · **Spec:** §16 · ⛔ **Safety: rule 7** · **Files:** `packages/knowledge/src/audit/validation-refusal.ts`, `packages/knowledge/src/gcl/visibility-gate.ts`
⛔ **THE GAP:** refs are **deduped then capped at 20 with the drop reported** — so **CARDINALITY is bounded and individual ref LENGTH is not.** ⇒ ***when a path cut fails, the failure mode is a COMPLETE path in the signal rather than a truncated one*** — which is exactly what `### 24.103`'s line-terminator leak produced.
⭐ **THE ARGUMENT FOR IT IS THE LEAK THAT ALREADY HAPPENED, NOT A HYPOTHETICAL: the cut is the only thing standing between a row-authored key and the signal, `isRedactionSafe` measurably does NOT backstop it (it returned `true` on the leaked codename), and a length clamp degrades ANY future cut failure to truncation.** ⚠ **NOT a substitute for the cut** — a clamp on a leaked path still leaks its prefix; it bounds the blast radius and is worth having for that alone.
**Done-when:** each ref is length-clamped with the clamp stated in-file and its **reason** (bounding a cut failure, not preventing one); ⛔ **the clamp must not silently truncate without the truncation being visible** — a silently shortened ref reads as a complete one (`L86`'s reported-drop discipline). *(origin: 2026-08-18, `### 24.103` Step 9)*

### 24.119 — a LINE TERMINATOR in a row-authored key silently defeated `### 24.103`'s region cut, and `isRedactionSafe` returned `true` on the result

- [x] DONE · `324a068d` · 2026-08-18 · ⛔ **STATE: FIXED** (the one word the lead required) — found by `security-reviewer` at `### 24.103` Step 8, **reproduced independently by knowledge-implementer before fixing** · **Track:** knowledge (`packages/knowledge`)
**Kind:** finding (fixed) · **Spec:** §16, §6 · ⛔ **Safety: rule 7** · **Files:** `packages/knowledge/src/audit/validation-refusal.ts`
⚠ **ENTRY TEXT AUTHORED BY knowledge-implementer IN THEIR OWN WORDS, LANDED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR** — the tracker is hook-enforced against implementer writes, so they could not land it themselves.
**1 — MECHANISM.** The cut was compiled with `"u"` ONLY ⇒ **`.` does not match a line terminator** (`\n`, `\r`, U+2028, U+2029) **and `$` without `m` matches only at end of input**, so a row-authored key containing one makes the **whole pattern fail to match** — and `structuralPathOnly`'s `?? path` fallback returns the path **VERBATIM.** ⛔ **That fallback is the exact fail-open the module's own header names as "the tempting implementation."** Fixed by adding `s`; dotAll only lets the lazy prefix find the region MORE often — the fail-safe direction.
**2 — THE BOUND. MEASURED:** with `s` absent all four schemas leaked the uncut path **including the GCL control**; `buildRefusalSignal` placed it in `refs`; **`isRedactionSafe` returned `true`** on the result. Trailing-terminator-as-final-character also leaked. ⇒ **detection provably could not have backstopped it; the cut IS the control.** **ALSO MEASURED:** the four live regions emit `additionalProperties:{}` with no `propertyNames`, Zod side `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` ⇒ neither validator can raise a per-entry issue under them today.
⚠ **INFERRED, AND WEAKER — SAID SO EXPLICITLY:** that *therefore* no row-authored key reaches `issue.path` in production. **That is a claim about every current producer; the four regions' DECLARATIONS were enumerated, not every path that can construct a `RefusalIssue`.** **No live leak demonstrated; none ruled out by exhaustion either.**
**3 — WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT:** a schema tightening giving a region a real subschema · a **key** constraint on a region (⚠ see `### 24.103`'s `L103` answer — it CREATES this vector rather than removing it) · any producer building a `RefusalIssue.path` from row-derived data outside these four validators.
**4 — STATE: FIXED**, regression-pinned over all four terminators, both dialects, full assembly, trailing-terminator. **Mutation-proven: drop `s` → exactly that pin reds** (mutation verified applied by diff first).
**5 — ⛔ WHICH KIND OF FAILURE, because *"caught by review"* hides it: A DEFECT *IN THE CONTROL*.** The cut was miswritten and **silently no-op'd** on a class of inputs — not a control firing and something slipping past. ⇒ ***the tests were WRONG, not vacuous: the row-key pin asserted something real, but its sentinel contained no terminator, so it passed identically on broken and fixed code.*** **The one direction never sampled, again.**
⭐ **CONTRAST, so the round's two kinds do not merge: the three decorative pins in the same slice were the OTHER category — VACUOUS, asserting nothing at all.** ⛔ **Different remedies: a WRONG control needs a new INPUT CLASS; a VACUOUS pin needs an ASSERTION THAT CAN FAIL.** ⚠ **A defective control is worse than an absent one, because the round it protects reads as covered — and this one did, through a fully green suite.** *(origin: 2026-08-18, `### 24.103` Step 8)*

The same literal `ok` now appears on `commit`, so the wrapper is VERB-AGNOSTIC and every `git` output surface is suspect**

⚠ **THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, STATED BECAUSE IT IS THE PART THAT COSTS SOMEONE A SESSION: *"DID MY COMMIT LAND?"* CANNOT BE ANSWERED FROM `git commit`'S OWN OUTPUT IN THIS CHECKOUT.** **Confirm with `git show --numstat` or `git rev-list`.** ⛔⛔ **AND THE DIRECTION IS THE NASTIEST OF THE SIX, SO IT GETS ITS OWN SENTENCE: `ok` READ LIKE SUCCESS AND *WAS* SUCCESS.** ⇒ ***the hazard is not a false alarm — it is a reader who learns `ok` means fine, and then meets it on a verb where it is NOT.*** ⭐ **A MISLEADING OUTPUT THAT HAPPENS TO BE TRUE TRAINS THE WRONG REFLEX MORE EFFECTIVELY THAN ONE THAT IS FALSE, because nothing ever contradicts it while the reflex is forming.**

### 24.139 — ⛔⛔ `sow-doctor` REPORTED A FINDING AND EXITED 1 ON A PERFECTLY HEALTHY INSTALL, FOREVER — a check the standalone CLI structurally cannot take

- [x] DONE · `6af3ee1d` · 2026-08-28 · found 2026-08-28 by an adversarial defect sweep (8 of 9 candidates refuted; this one **reproduced end-to-end before any fix** — a maximally healthy fake machine printed ten `[ok]` lines, then `[finding] single_owner_lock`, `overall: finding`, exit 1) · **Depends:** — · **Blocks:** — · **Track:** worker (`apps/worker`) + contract (`packages/contracts`)
**Kind:** fix · **Spec:** §13, §16 · ⛔ **Safety: rule 1 posture surface — and the failure mode is a FALSE ALARM, which is the direction nobody audits** · **Files:** `apps/worker/src/install/doctor.ts` · `doctor-cli.ts` · `probe-collectors.ts` · `checks/environment.ts` · `lock/singleOwnerLockDoctorCheck.ts` · `packages/contracts/src/install/doctor-result.ts` · `packages/evals/src/install/clean-install.acceptance.ts`
⛔ **THE MECHANISM:** `single_owner_lock` joined `runDoctor`'s check array at `eed76756` (2026-08-25). `doctor-cli.ts` had not been touched since 2026-07-11 and never supplied the probe. **Every field on `ProbeSnapshot` is OPTIONAL, so `Partial<ProbeSnapshot>` type-checked cleanly and nothing caught the omission** — the compiler enumeration that secures the rest of this codebase was structurally absent here. `diagnoseSingleOwnerLock(undefined)` fails closed to `single_owner_lock_not_held`, `rollUpStatus` takes worst-of, `doctorExitCode` returns 1. Same gap in `runPrerequisiteDoctor` (`probe-collectors.ts:260`).
⛔⛔ **THE FIX IS NOT "POPULATE THE FIELD", AND THAT IS THE WHOLE FINDING.** `sow-doctor` is a **SEPARATE PROCESS**; the probe is BY DEFINITION the outcome of the worker's boot-time `acquireSingleOwnerLock`. A standalone CLI can neither read it nor substitute for it — ***acquiring the lock itself would report a finding exactly when a healthy worker holds it, and `ok` exactly when none is running. The INVERSE of the truth.***
⭐⭐ **ROOT CAUSE IS A TAXONOMY DEFECT (`worker L79`): *"not held"* and *"cannot be observed from here"* are DIFFERENT STATES, and only the first is a VERDICT.** Remedy: an additive-optional `lockObservable` on `runDoctor`; a standalone process passes `false` and receives `degraded` + a NEW `single_owner_lock_not_observable` variant pointing at the running worker's System Health — **never `ok`** (nothing was proven), **never `_not_held`** (nothing was measured). The contract requires a variant on any non-`ok` status, so *"no variant"* was not available and borrowing one that asserts a verdict is `### 24.67`'s rejected move.
✅ **THE FAIL-CLOSED RULE IS UNCHANGED AND STILL RIGHT** — default and `lockObservable: true` are byte-equivalent, pinned by a non-vacuity test over omitted / `{}` / explicit `true`, plus a genuinely-unheld lock still reporting a finding.
⚠ **TWO DOC BLOCKS WERE STALE IN THE REASSURING DIRECTION AND ARE CORRECTED IN THE SAME COMMIT** — `singleOwnerLockDoctorCheck.ts` still read *"NOT YET WIRED"* three days after it was wired, ⇒ ***a reader auditing why the doctor was red would have ruled this check out because the file says it does not run***; and `clean-install.acceptance.ts`'s gap note asserted the doctor *"never reports a lock finding even on a genuine refusal"* — the exact opposite of shipped behaviour.
⭐ **WHY IT SURVIVED THREE DAYS OF GREEN SUITES:** every `runInstallDoctor` test injects faults (so a finding is expected), the `SOW_DOCTOR_REAL` end-to-end asserts only `[0,1]).toContain(code)`, and the eval suite's `ALL_OK` fixture sets `singleOwnerLock: { acquired: true }` by hand. ⇒ ***no test anywhere drove the SHIPPED composition root over a healthy machine***, which is the one scenario the binary exists for. *(origin: 2026-08-28 defect sweep)*
